title: Aureum Vellus: Guldin Schatz und Kunstkammer with Splendor Solis illustrations (Cod. Sang. 1727)
shelf_note: A German alchemical manuscript in a 17th-century cursive hand (a recipe for a 'gradier' process). It matches the catalogue description. No collection is set, so there is nothing to contradict.
structure_note: The leaf carries pencil foliation '196' and is record 200, an offset of 4, which is plausible for front matter. printed_backsteps 59 and printed_repeats 62 out of 432 numbered pages is high. It more likely reflects a pencil numbering that the OCR misread or that the volume restarts (a compiled codex) than a scan splice, but this one page cannot settle it. structure.pages_translated is 0 while pages_translated_field is 517, so the counts disagree.

pages.layout: single column of cursive text in a ruled frame; two-line title repeated above the frame; alchemical symbols inline; catchword 'das' at foot right

ocr_errors.image: Process Eines geheimen gradier ▽ (a downward triangle, the water sign, in both title lines)
ocr_errors.problem: The water sign is transcribed as the fire sign (🜂 is an upward triangle). The process is a grading water ('Gradierwasser'), not a fire.

ocr_errors.image: Jm ▽ man darin Baad dz ☉ (again a downward triangle)
ocr_errors.problem: The water sign is read as mercury, which changes the medium of the bath.

ocr_errors.image: ℞ 3 lot ☉, das Laminier (numeral '3' with ditto marks, then 'lot')
ocr_errors.problem: The quantity '3 lot' of gold is replaced by 'Halbe' (half). This is a dose error.

ocr_errors.ocr: Und folgt in Parafolon dz Stuhls
ocr_errors.image: Und Volgt in Parasolon, dz Stuckh, (apparently 'Stuck/Stück', piece)
ocr_errors.problem: 'Stuhls' (chair) for what looks like 'Stuckh' (piece/item). The misreading yields nonsense.

ocr_errors.image: the numeral before 'Lot' looks like the scribe's 'z'-shaped 2, written between ditto marks like the '2' elsewhere on the page
ocr_errors.problem: The quantity may be misread (7½ vs 2). The hand is hard to read here, so confidence is low.

tr_errors.problem: Built on the misread sign. The image has the water sign, so this is a 'grading water'. The note gives the error a confident, authoritative explanation.

tr_errors.english: In mercury ☿ one bathes the gold ☉ therein
tr_errors.problem: The image reads water (▽), not mercury. The OCR misreading is carried into the English, which gives the wrong medium.
The image gives a weight, '3 lot' of gold. 'Half' loses the dose.

tr_errors.problem: 'of the chair' comes from the 'Stuhls' misreading. The note speculates instead of flagging the reading as doubtful.

missing.why: A general reader will not know a cucurbit is the gourd-shaped lower vessel of an alembic for distillation.
Cementation, heating metal packed in a reactive powder, is a technical assaying term the reader needs explained.

missing.english: Let it macerate in hot sand, up to 2 🜔.
missing.why: The symbol after '2' is left unexplained, so the duration or quantity of the step cannot be followed. The image shows a boxed-X sign, not the salt sign.

book_verdict: This is the right leaf, a fair transcription of a hard cursive hand, and a fluent English version. But the alchemical signs are misread at the points that matter: water is read as fire and as mercury, and '3 lot' of gold becomes 'half'. A confident note then explains the wrong sign as fire, so the recipe reaches the reader with the wrong substances and dose.
